hints: Notice both ropes pull upward at different angles, so only the vertical parts $T\sin\theta$ can balance the weight.
For equilibrium the vector sum is zero, so $410\sin60^{\circ}+210\sin10^{\circ} - mg = 0$ with $g = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Calculate $410\sin60^{\circ}$ and $210\sin10^{\circ}$ separately, add them to get the weight, then divide by $9.81$ to get mass in $\text{kg}$.
walkthrough: The object is in equilibrium, so upward forces must balance the downward weight $W = mg$. Only vertical components of the $410 \text{ N}$ and $210 \text{ N}$ tensions act upward.
Resolve each tension vertically using $T_{v} = T\sin\theta$ because the given $60^{\circ}$ and $10^{\circ}$ are to the horizontal.
Substitute values with units: $T_{1v} = 410\sin60^{\circ} \approx 355.1 \text{ N}$ and $T_{2v} = 210\sin10^{\circ} \approx 36.5 \text{ N}$.
Add for total upward force: $W = 355.1 + 36.5 \approx 391.6 \text{ N}$.
Use $m = W/g$: $m = 391.6/9.81 \approx 39.9 \text{ kg}$, about $40 \text{ kg}$ with sensible precision. This is option A.

options.A: The summed upward components are about $392 \text{ N}$, so $m = 392/9.81$ gives about $40 \text{ kg}$.
options.B: This is slightly too large and does not match $410\sin60^{\circ}+210\sin10^{\circ}$ divided by $9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
options.C: This mistakes the total upward force in newtons, about $392 \text{ N}$, for the mass without dividing by $g$.
options.D: This mistakes a tension value in newtons for the mass and ignores resolving both tensions into vertical components.
